Rejection root-cause analysis and fix (session herdr-1791389893-1978007-18263).

Root cause of the operator's rejection ("oscillates with left and right rotation thrusters", "firing semi-randomly"): the bot returned only a cardinal (N/E/S/W) steering intent. Under the shipped asteroids controls the governor then turned the hull to a cardinal (open-loop for the 250 ms reaction window), so it could never point at an off-axis target and hunted/overshot between cardinals; the danger-margin approach/retreat also flipped at the boundary.

Fix:
- `decideBotIntent` (new) returns the four-directional cardinal projection PLUS the precise unit bearing to the chosen target (`dirX`/`dirY`). `decideBotInput` remains as the four-directional projection for the `fourDirectional` scheme/legacy callers. The precise bearing is validated by the survival tier (generalised `evaluateDirection` -> `evaluateVector`) and falls back to the best safe cardinal when blocked.
- `toAsteroidsInput` aims the hull at the precise bearing (cardinal fallback when absent).
- `BotInputGovernor` now holds the committed *intent* but re-resolves it against the ship's current facing every tick (closed-loop turn), so a held "aim at the mineral" command tracks the target and never overshoots.
- Engagement hysteresis (`engagementHysteresis` tunable) damps the approach/retreat flip-flop at the danger margin.

Evidence: deterministic closed-loop simulation (`src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts`, no Phaser) shows the ship points at an off-axis mineral (non-cardinal bearing within 0.35 rad) and closes on it, and targets an off-axis enemy; 70 AI tests and the full 3527-test suite pass; typecheck and build clean.
